title: Vault chunked NFT generation with progress, cancel, and large-run rendering safeguards

requirements.summary: Chunk Vault collection generation into batches and yield to the UI between batches to prevent freezes on 10k+ runs.
acceptanceCriteria: Generating a collection of 10,000 NFTs does not cause the UI to freeze for extended periods; the browser remains interactive during generation.
Generation work yields to the event loop at least once per batch (e.g., via requestAnimationFrame, setTimeout(0), or equivalent) so progress updates and user input are processed.

file_operations.description: Add a small utility to yield execution back to the browser event loop (e.g., requestAnimationFrame/setTimeout) so long-running generation can remain responsive.
Refactor generateCollection to run in configurable batches and await a yield-to-UI helper after each batch so state updates, rendering, and user interactions are processed between batches.

requirements.summary: Progressively commit generated NFTs to the project after each batch via onUpdateProject, clearing once at start and sorting/updating timestamp at end.
acceptanceCriteria: At the start of a new generation run, the project.generatedNFTs list is cleared immediately (replace-only behavior remains).
During generation, project.generatedNFTs grows incrementally in batches (observable in UI item count) rather than only appearing at the end.
After completion, generatedNFTs are sorted by token id as they are today and lastGeneratedAt is updated.

file_operations.description: Change generation state handling to: (1) clear generatedNFTs once at run start; (2) commit forged tokens immediately; (3) append each batch’s newly generated NFTs via onUpdateProject without accumulating a large in-function array; (4) on completion, perform a final onUpdateProject to sort by token id and set lastGeneratedAt.

requirements.summary: Add in-generation progress UI (percent + counts) and a Cancel control that stops generation within one batch while keeping already-generated NFTs usable.
acceptanceCriteria: While generating, the UI shows a continuously updating progress indicator with both percent and counts generated/target.
A Cancel button is visible only while generation is in progress.
Cancel stops further generation quickly (within one batch) and leaves any already-generated NFTs intact and usable (can be viewed/exported).
After cancel, the Generate button becomes usable again without requiring a tab switch or navigation.

file_operations.description: Add generation-run control state (e.g., a cancel ref/run id) and UI elements to display percent plus “generated / target” counts during generation, and a Cancel button shown only while generating that requests cancellation and is checked between batches so the run stops safely.

requirements.summary: Add an optional headless/low-memory mode toggle near Vault generation controls to reduce rendering work during 10k–20k runs (default off).
acceptanceCriteria: A user-facing toggle (English text) is available near the Generate control to enable/disable headless/low-memory mode.
When enabled, Vault avoids expensive live rendering during the run (e.g., suppress/placeholder the grid rendering while generating, or equivalent) while still generating NFTs.
When generation finishes or is canceled, normal Vault rendering resumes automatically.

file_operations.description: Add a headless/low-memory mode toggle (default off) to the Vault generation controls and use it to suppress expensive preview rendering while a run is in progress; ensure normal rendering is restored automatically on completion/cancel.

requirements.summary: Add Vault rendering safeguards so large generatedNFTs lists (and in-progress runs) do not lock the UI from rendering thousands of thumbnails.
acceptanceCriteria: During generation, Vault does not attempt to render the full grid of thumbnails in a way that causes noticeable lockups.
After generation completes, the Vault grid becomes usable and scrollable; thumbnails display as expected.

file_operations.description: Implement large-list rendering safeguards: during generation show a lightweight “Generating…” view (and avoid mapping thousands of nodes), and for very large collections gate thumbnail rendering with a lightweight mode (e.g., render-limited/paged thumbnails or a user-controlled ‘show thumbnails’ action) to keep the UI responsive.

requirements.summary: Preserve determinism, rules validation, uniqueness, and forged-token integration across the chunked/progressive generation pipeline (including partial completion warnings).
acceptanceCriteria: Generated NFTs continue to respect project.rules via isValidCombination checks.
No duplicate DNA values are introduced within a run (uniqueness is maintained across batches).
Forged tokens are included as before and still reserve token numbers appropriately.
If the generator cannot reach targetCount within maxAttempts, the UI reports partial completion (existing warning behavior preserved), and the app remains responsive.

file_operations.description: Ensure the batched generator maintains a single run-scoped uniqueness set across batches, continues to apply isValidCombination checks, integrates forged tokens up-front with reserved token numbers, and preserves partial-completion warning behavior when maxAttempts is reached—while still yielding to the UI between batches.
